title: Whitney's C^1 extension theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6)
statement: Let n be a natural number, A ⊆ R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) a closed set, h : R^n -> R, and D : R^n -> L(R^n,R) (continuous linear maps). Assume that h and D are continuous on A, and that (*) for every compact Q ⊆ A and every η > 0 there is ρ > 0 with |h(y) - h(x) - D(x)(y - x)| <= η |y - x| for all x ∈ Q and all y ∈ A with dist(x, y) < ρ. Then there is a function g : R^n -> R of class C^1 (ContDiff R 1 g) such that g(a) = h(a) and g is differentiable at a with derivative D(a) (HasFDerivAt g (D a) a), for every a ∈ A.
lean_statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (A : Set (Rn n)) (h : Rn n → ℝ) (D : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] ℝ)), IsClosed A → ContinuousOn h A → ContinuousOn D A → (∀ Q : Set (Rn n), IsCompact Q → Q ⊆ A → ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ∀ x ∈ Q, ∀ y ∈ A, dist x y < ρ → ‖h y - h x - D x (y - x)‖ ≤ η * ‖y - x‖) → ∃ g : Rn n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ (∀ a ∈ A, g a = h a) ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, HasFDerivAt g (D a) a
